SAS SYMGET(argument)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_symget.Rd

Value of a macro variable at run time. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

symtab

Macro symbol table to look the variable up in (an environment or macro session supplied by the generated code; not part of the SAS syntax).

name

Character name of the macro variable, not case sensitive; trailing blanks are ignored. A blank or invalid name gives a blank result with a note in the log.

.at

Internal: source position c(line, column) used in log NOTEs.

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

Reads the macro symbol table of the running SAS program.

Examples

# SYMGET: each call is explained above it and followed by its result

# SYMGET returns the value of the macro variable mv, which was set with a LET
# statement.
sas_f_symget(list2env(list(mv = "hello")), "mv")  # symget('mv') = "hello"
#> [1] "hello"

# Macro variable names are not case sensitive.
sas_f_symget(list2env(list(mv = "hello")), "MV")  # symget('MV') = "hello"
#> [1] "hello"

# A name with a leading blank is invalid, so the result is blank (with a note
# in the log).
sas_f_symget(list2env(list(mv = "hello")), " mv ")  # symget(' mv ') = ""
#> Warning: NOTE: Invalid argument to function SYMGET(' mv ').
#> [1] ""
